children: The Hang Seng Index has remained in a correction after falling by over 15% from its highest point this year. This retreat will be put to the test this week as some of the biggest Chinese companies publish their earnings reports. Some of the most notable ones are Baidu, Trip.com, Alibaba, Tencent, and Lenovo Group.
Alibaba Group to publish earnings as stock crashes

Alibaba, one of the biggest companies in China, will be in the spotlight this week as it releases its financial results. BABA was trading at $90.5 in Hong Kong, down by over 50% from its highest point in October last year. It has slumped to its lowest level since June this year.
Alibaba has decoupled from Amazon, a company that uses a similar business model. Its stock has plunged by over 70% from its all-time high, even as Amazon has moved close to its all-time high.

Alibaba’s performance has been dragged by the rising AI spending that has pushed the management to issue shares. It recently raised $10 billion in a fundraising that diluted its shareholders. Also, the company’s profits have dived in the past few quarters. Its net income dropped by 75% in the second quarter to $1.53 billion.
Tencent Holdings to release earnings as its stock drops

Tencent Holdings, a top Chinese conglomerate that owns brands like Riot Games, WeChat, Funom, and stakes in Epic Games, Ubisoft, and PDD, has also plunged this year. It was trading at $386, down by over 43% from its highest point in October last year. It has slumped to its lowest level since January last year.

Like Alibaba, Tencent’s business is being affected by the rising AI investments that have hurt its profits. The last results showed that its revenue rose by 11% in the second quarter to RMB 204.8 billion, while the net profit rose by 9% to RMB 70.6 billion.
Notably, Tencent’s capital expenditure jumped by 176% to RMB 52.8 billion. The company raised $5.7 billion in debt to continue its AI spending.
Lenovo Group stock has dropped because of AI jitters
Lenovo Group is another top Hang Seng stock to watch this week as it releases its earnings. These earnings come at a time when the company’s stock has plunged by 53% from its all-time high.

Lenovo has plunged because of the ongoing jitters surrounding the artificial intelligence (AI) industry. Its retreat has mirrored the performance of other popular companies like Dell and HP Enterprise.

Unlike Alibaba and Tencent, Lenovo Group’s business is doing well, with revenue, profits, and backlog continuing to rise. Its last earnings report showed that its revenue soared to over $26.9 billion, up by 43% from a year earlier. This growth was driven by a 60% increase in its AI business.

Lenovo’s business is benefiting from the ongoing data center spending that has pushed to a significant increase in demand for its servers and storage products. Based on the recent earnings by its hyperscaler clients and competitors, chances are that Lenovo will publish strong numbers.

The challenge, however, is that there are jitters that the AI bubble is about to burst, which will affect its revenue growth in the future. On the positive side, if these concerns are overblown, then there is a likelihood that the ongoing retreat has made it a good bargain.
Baidu stock has plunged ahead of earnings

Baidu, which is seen as China’s version of Google, has plunged to $74.20 in Hong Kong. It has fallen from the year-to-date high of $160 amid concerns about the AI industry and its impact on its business.

One of the top concerns about the company is its Kunluxin IPO, which is expected to be delayed to next year. Also, investors are concerned about the impact of AI search on its business. In its recent results, Google said that AI search was more difficult to monetize than traditional search.
Baidu will publish its earnings report on Monday, and analysts expect it to show that its revenue growth stalled, while AI costs soared.

title: Hang Seng Index in focus ahead of Baidu, Alibaba, Tencent, Lenovo earnings
